author: pro_review

public_api.writer: sealed_payload(raw: bytes) -> context manager yielding one owned descriptor
public_api.reader: read_sealed_payload(fd: int, expected_sha256: str) -> bytes; descriptor borrowed, never closed
protocol: Linux os.memfd_create uses MFD_CLOEXEC | MFD_ALLOW_SEALING. There is no pipe or temporary-file fallback.
Bounded positive-progress write loop rejects zero, invalid length and I/O errors. Before yielding, F_SEAL_WRITE | F_SEAL_GROW | F_SEAL_SHRINK | F_SEAL_SEAL are applied and checked using F_GET_SEALS.
Writer reads the complete sealed bytes back and verifies SHA-256 before yield. No process is created by the module.
Reader checks a regular file, nonempty bounded size, all four seals, exact bytes/hash, and matching fstat identity before/after. pread leaves shared offset unchanged.
Writer context closes its descriptor once, including preparation/body errors. An uncertain close raises sealed_payload_close_failed and is not retried against a potentially reused descriptor.

The context must span prepare_supervised(worker_only_fds=(fd,)) until worker fork. A fixed caller driver must close the inherited FD after verification and before importing an adapter. Only FD number and expected digest need enter command arguments; payload bytes do not.

groups.coverage: Real seals reject pwrite, file growth, file shrink and shared writable mmap; content remains identical, FD is CLOEXEC and context closes it.
Both exact 1-byte and 65536-byte boundaries read correctly. Read/hash-mismatch leaves caller FD live and shared offset unchanged.

Actual prepare_supervised inherits worker-only sealed FD. Parent exits its context after READY and before GO; the actual worker still reads identical Unicode/NUL/non-UTF8 bytes, closes its copy and exits with exact TREE_CLOSED proof. No database or posthoc adapter is claimed.
None, str, bytearray, bytes subclass, empty and oversized values reject before memfd creation.
Boolean/stdio FD and noncanonical/nonstring digest reject before descriptor I/O or close.
Unsealed memfd, WRITE-only seal and pipe reject while retaining caller ownership.
Real descriptor with zero-write, actual positive partial write followed by EIO, seal syscall failure, or short readback. No context yield; exactly one close.

groups.kind: explicit close fault with real descriptor reuse
groups.coverage: Close actually releases FD, a new devnull descriptor immediately reuses the number, then close raises. Replacement remains live; no second close is attempted.
Missing memfd_create fails closed without an alternate transport.

tests.evidence_boundary: Real-kernel/CPU assertions and selected syscall/capability doubles are separated explicitly. The new API was implemented before these tests were first executed; import absence was never counted as a failure.

integration_handoff.close_after_spawn_warning: Context exit can fail after prepare has forked a worker. The caller must save that created handle inside the context before exit and retain/stop it through existing supervision authority; SealedPayloadError at that point does not prove NOT_STARTED.
parent_responsibilities: Build/validate payload before creation and retain its exact digest.
Pass the borrowed FD explicitly as worker_only_fds, retaining context until prepare returns.
Save any created handle before context exit; unknown close/spawn state follows owned STOP/HOLD rather than blind retry.
Fixed driver verifies sealed bytes, closes inherited descriptor before adapter imports, and separately enforces genuine attempt/scope/native publication authority.

limitations: Linux local in-memory immutable bytes, not durable storage, artifact registration, observation validity or crash recovery.
Descriptor owner must not concurrently close/reassign the borrowed FD during reading/preparation. Stable FD number alone is not persistent execution authority.
This module performs no SQLite admission, native posthoc policy, adapter loading, Popen, signalling, provider call or process recovery.
The actual CPU roundtrip tests generic supervisor inheritance, not the later fixed posthoc driver or the complete native posthoc workflow.
No real GPU, model training, paid provider, holdout or host process scan was used. No research-efficiency or whole-V1 completion claim.
The helper's constructor and read functions fail closed, but a caller integrating context exit after spawn must preserve its actual process ownership; the bytes module cannot resolve that externally.
